title: Clear-To-List Baseline Requirements — All States
content:
Clear-To-List (CTL) Determination Policy — Baseline Requirements Applicable to All U.S. States and Territories.

Purpose: The CTL determination is the final gate before a distressed residential property may be marketed for sale. It ensures that all legal, valuation, occupancy, and compliance prerequisites are satisfied before public listing. Properties that fail the CTL gate must not be listed until all blocking conditions are resolved.

Section 1 — Title Clearance:
A property may not be listed unless its title is clear of all material encumbrances that would prevent lawful conveyance to a buyer. Material encumbrances include: unreleased mortgage liens, federal or state tax liens, mechanic's liens exceeding $2,500, judgment liens, and lis pendens filings. Minor encumbrances such as utility easements, standard restrictive covenants, and recorded homestead exemptions do not block listing. Title must be verified through an accredited title search provider within 60 days of listing.

Section 2 — Valuation Requirement:
Every property must have a current valuation before listing. The primary valuation instrument is the Broker Price Opinion (BPO). A BPO is considered current if completed within 90 days unless a stricter state-specific threshold applies. If no current BPO exists, a new BPO must be ordered before listing may proceed. An Automated Valuation Model (AVM) should be obtained as a secondary reference. If AVM-to-BPO variance exceeds 15 percent, the property must be flagged for manual valuation review before listing.

Section 3 — Occupancy Verification:
Property occupancy status must be confirmed via field inspection within the most recent 30-day period. A vacant, secured property is clear for listing. An occupied property requires resolution through lawful eviction proceedings or voluntary vacancy programs before listing. Any property with unknown occupancy status must undergo field inspection before CTL determination.
Pre-Verified Occupancy Exemption: If the asset profile already shows a confirmed Vacant occupancy status AND the asset was ingested into the system within the last 7 days, occupancy verification is considered pre-satisfied. In this case the Occupancy and Condition domain investigation SHOULD BE OMITTED from the verification plan because the data is current and non-blocking. This exemption applies only to Tier 2 sellers. Tier 1 sellers require all conditions fully satisfied and must always undergo full occupancy investigation. Tier 3 sellers and any asset with Occupied or Unknown status must also always undergo full occupancy investigation.

Section 4 — Code and Compliance:
All critical municipal code violations (structural, health, safety) must be resolved before listing. Non-critical violations such as cosmetic issues, minor landscaping, or non-habitable accessory structures may be listed with condition disclosure. Properties with unresolved condemnation orders are not eligible for listing.

Section 5 — HOA Status:
If the property is subject to a Homeowners Association, assess current standing. Outstanding HOA assessments exceeding five thousand dollars constitute a CTL blocker requiring resolution. Assessments between one thousand and five thousand dollars allow conditional listing with buyer disclosure. Assessments below one thousand dollars do not block listing. Estoppel certificates must be requested as part of the closing process.

Section 6 — Confidence Scoring:
The CTL determination produces a confidence score between 0.0 and 1.0. Scores at or above 0.90 indicate a Clear verdict. Scores between 0.75 and 0.89 indicate ClearWithConditions, meaning the property may be listed with specific conditions disclosed. Scores below 0.75 indicate NeedsHumanReview, requiring an asset manager to manually evaluate the property before any listing decision.

Section 7 — Seller Tier Impact:
Seller tier classification affects CTL processing. Tier 1 sellers (institutional with high volume and contractual SLAs) require all conditions to be fully satisfied before listing — conditional listing is not permitted. Tier 2 sellers allow conditional listing for non-blocking issues. Tier 3 sellers (individual or small portfolio) follow standard baseline rules.

References: This policy incorporates requirements consistent with HUD servicing guidelines, Regulation X (12 CFR Part 1024), and standard industry practices for distressed asset disposition.
